claim: ACP1 is essential for cell viability in multiple Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain backgrounds.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, ACP1, the gene encoding ACP, is essential for cell viability in multiple strain backgrounds, while the genes required for lipoic acid biosynthesis and ligation are not (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C) (Schonauer et al., 2008; Brody et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C, and cited references.

claim: Genes required for lipoic acid biosynthesis and ligation are not essential for cell viability in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, ACP1, the gene encoding ACP, is essential for cell viability in multiple strain backgrounds, while the genes required for lipoic acid biosynthesis and ligation are not (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C) (Schonauer et al., 2008; Brody et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C, and cited references.

claim: ACP is essential for viability in Yarrowia lipolytica.
source: This is consistent with reports demonstrating that ACP is essential for viability in Yarrowia lipolytica (Dobrynin et al., 2010) and in mammalian cells (Yi and Maeda, 2005; Feng et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: ACP is essential for viability in mammalian cells.
source: This is consistent with reports demonstrating that ACP is essential for viability in Yarrowia lipolytica (Dobrynin et al., 2010) and in mammalian cells (Yi and Maeda, 2005; Feng et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: Saccharomyces cerevisiae mitochondria do not have Complex I or any structurally similar analog of it.
source: Moreover, S. cerevisiae mitochondria do not have CI or any structurally similar analog of it.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about S. cerevisiae mitochondria.

claim: Acp1 co-purifies with three subunits of the ISU complex: Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1.
source: We were particularly intrigued by the co-purification of three subunits of the ISU complex—Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1—each of which is required for FeS biogenesis and essential for viability.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from purification experiments.

claim: Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1 are each required for FeS biogenesis and essential for viability.
source: We were particularly intrigued by the co-purification of three subunits of the ISU complex—Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1—each of which is required for FeS biogenesis and essential for viability.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about the ISU complex.

claim: Nfs1 and Isd11 form the core of the ISU complex.
source: The cysteine desulfurase (Nfs1) and Isd11 form the core of the ISU complex and catalyze the conversion of cysteine to alanine thereby generating a persulfide intermediate, which is the source of sulfide ions that combine with ferrous iron on the Isu1 scaffold protein to form [2Fe-2S] clusters (Garland et al., 1999; Mühlenhoff et al., 2004; Adam et al., 2006; Wiedemann et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: The ISU complex catalyzes the conversion of cysteine to alanine thereby generating a persulfide intermediate.
source: The cysteine desulfurase (Nfs1) and Isd11 form the core of the ISU complex and catalyze the conversion of cysteine to alanine thereby generating a persulfide intermediate, which is the source of sulfide ions that combine with ferrous iron on the Isu1 scaffold protein to form [2Fe-2S] clusters (Garland et al., 1999; Mühlenhoff et al., 2004; Adam et al., 2006; Wiedemann et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: The persulfide intermediate is the source of sulfide ions that combine with ferrous iron on the Isu1 scaffold protein to form [2Fe-2S] clusters.
source: The cysteine desulfurase (Nfs1) and Isd11 form the core of the ISU complex and catalyze the conversion of cysteine to alanine thereby generating a persulfide intermediate, which is the source of sulfide ions that combine with ferrous iron on the Isu1 scaffold protein to form [2Fe-2S] clusters (Garland et al., 1999; Mühlenhoff et al., 2004; Adam et al., 2006; Wiedemann et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1 specifically co-immunoprecipitate with Acp1.
source: Indeed, Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1 all specifically co-immunoprecipitate with Acp1, although Isu1 appears to interact less avidly than Nfs1 or Isd11 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Isu1 appears to interact less avidly with Acp1 than Nfs1 or Isd11.
source: Indeed, Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1 all specifically co-immunoprecipitate with Acp1, although Isu1 appears to interact less avidly than Nfs1 or Isd11 (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Acp1 co-purifies with the intact core Nfs1-Isd11 complex.
source: In addition to SDS-PAGE, the resultant eluates were also resolved by blue native (BN)-PAGE, which demonstrated that Acp1 co-purifies with the intact core Nfs1-Isd11 complex (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Human ACP, NFS1, and ISD11 are mutually interacting proteins in mammalian cells.
source: These results are further supported by proteomics-based interaction studies, which identify human ACP, NFS1, and ISD11 as mutually interacting proteins in mammalian cells (Huttlin et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Acp1 is a stable and evolutionarily conserved subunit of the ISU complex with Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1.
source: Taken together these data demonstrate that Acp1 is a stable and evolutionarily conserved subunit of the ISU complex with Nfs1, Isd11, and Isu1.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing co-purification and co-immunoprecipitation, and supported by proteomics studies.

claim: FeS biogenesis is an essential function of mitochondria.
source: FeS biogenesis is an essential function of mitochondria and is absolutely dependent on the ISU complex with which Acp1 stably interacts (Lill et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: FeS biogenesis is absolutely dependent on the ISU complex.
source: FeS biogenesis is an essential function of mitochondria and is absolutely dependent on the ISU complex with which Acp1 stably interacts (Lill et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Acp1KD cells display attenuated growth upon ACP1 shutdown, particularly evident on respiration-requiring glycerol medium.
source: As expected, Acp1KD cells from each background displayed attenuated growth upon ACP1 shutdown, which is particularly evident on respiration-requiring glycerol medium (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Viability of Acp1KD cells can be restored by episomal expression of Acp1-HA at endogenous levels.
source: Importantly, viability could be restored in each of these strains by episomal expression of the Acp1-HA at endogenous levels.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from rescue experiments.

claim: Acp1KD cells exhibit a loss of lipoic acid-containing subunits of pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.
source: In addition to the expected loss of lipoic acid-containing subunits of pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase in the Acp1KD cells, we also observed a specific destabilization of the FeS-containing subunits of Complex II (Sdh2) and Complex III (Rip1) and loss of those assembled respiratory complexes (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Acp1KD cells exhibit a specific destabilization of the FeS-containing subunits of Complex II (Sdh2) and Complex III (Rip1).
source: In addition to the expected loss of lipoic acid-containing subunits of pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase in the Acp1KD cells, we also observed a specific destabilization of the FeS-containing subunits of Complex II (Sdh2) and Complex III (Rip1) and loss of those assembled respiratory complexes (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Acp1KD cells exhibit loss of assembled respiratory complexes II and III.
source: In addition to the expected loss of lipoic acid-containing subunits of pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase in the Acp1KD cells, we also observed a specific destabilization of the FeS-containing subunits of Complex II (Sdh2) and Complex III (Rip1) and loss of those assembled respiratory complexes (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A similar destabilization of respiratory complexes occurs in cells depleted for Nfs1 and Isu1.
source: A similar destabilization of these complexes occurs in cells depleted for Nfs1 and Isu1 (Adam et al., 2006; Wiedemann et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: Complex III biogenesis stalls in Acp1KD cells at the final stage of assembly – incorporation of the Rieske FeS protein (Rip1).
source: Importantly, Complex III biogenesis stalls in Acp1KD cells at the final stage of assembly – incorporation of the Rieske FeS protein (Rip1) (Figure 2A; IB: Rip1)–resulting in the accumulation of a stable assembly intermediate of Complex III lacking Rip1 (Figure 2A; III2*; IB: Qcr7).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Acp1KD cells accumulate a stable assembly intermediate of Complex III lacking Rip1.
source: Importantly, Complex III biogenesis stalls in Acp1KD cells at the final stage of assembly – incorporation of the Rieske FeS protein (Rip1) (Figure 2A; IB: Rip1)–resulting in the accumulation of a stable assembly intermediate of Complex III lacking Rip1 (Figure 2A; III2*; IB: Qcr7).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The presence of the late stage intermediate III2* indicates that mitochondrial translation of the Cob cytochrome b subunit is normal in Acp1KD cells.
source: The presence of the late stage intermediate III2* indicates that mitochondrial translation of the Cob cytochrome b subunit is normal in Acp1KD cells (Atkinson et al., 2011; Cui et al., 2012).
evidence: Inferred from the presence of the assembly intermediate, supported by cited references.

claim: Translation of the mitochondrial subunits of ATP synthase is normal in Acp1KD cells.
source: Likewise, translation of the mitochondrial subunits of ATP synthase is normal as seen by the assembled F1F0 complex (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Acp1KD cells exhibit a loss of activity of aconitase.
source: We also observed a loss of activity of aconitase, a mitochondrial enzyme with an obligate FeS cofactor (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Aconitase is a mitochondrial enzyme with an obligate FeS cofactor.
source: We also observed a loss of activity of aconitase, a mitochondrial enzyme with an obligate FeS cofactor (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about aconitase.

claim: The mitochondrial ISU complex is essential for the production of FeS that act in the cytosol.
source: The mitochondrial ISU complex is essential for the production of FeS that act in the cytosol as well as ribosome assembly (Kispal et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: The mitochondrial ISU complex is essential for ribosome assembly.
source: The mitochondrial ISU complex is essential for the production of FeS that act in the cytosol as well as ribosome assembly (Kispal et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Mitochondrial FeS synthesis is important to attenuate the transcriptional activity of two partially redundant iron-responsive factors Aft1 and Aft2.
source: In addition, mitochondrial FeS synthesis is important to attenuate the transcriptional activity of two partially redundant iron-responsive factors Aft1 and Aft2.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about iron regulation.

claim: In Acp1KD cells the expression of Aft1-target genes FIT2 and FIT3 was elevated consistent with impaired mitochondrial FeS synthesis.
source: In Acp1KD cells the expression of Aft1-target genes FIT2 and FIT3 was elevated consistent with impaired mitochondrial FeS synthesis (Figure 2C) (Chen et al., 2004; Rutherford et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and cited references.

claim: Aft1 target genes are induced in cells lacking the two mitochondrial iron transporters Mrs3 and Mrs4.
source: These Aft1 target genes are also induced in cells lacking the two mitochondrial iron transporters Mrs3 and Mrs4 (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Acp1KD cells exhibit a diminution in the activity of the cytosolic FeS-containing enzyme sulfite reductase.
source: To further assess the perturbation of cytosolic FeS function, we quantified the activity of the cytosolic FeS-containing enzyme sulfite reductase and observed a diminution in Acp1KD cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Acp1 is essential for FeS biogenesis.
source: Combined with the essential nature of ACP1, these data demonstrate that Acp1 is essential for FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the combined experimental data showing effects on FeS-containing proteins and enzymes.

claim: Acp1KD cells exhibit a marked diminution of the assembled Nfs1-Isd11 complex.
source: Acp1KD cells exhibited a marked diminution of the assembled Nfs1-Isd11 complex, similar to depletion of the other ISU complex subunits (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: In the absence of Acp1, the Nfs1 and Isd11 protein that remain are found only in insoluble aggregates.
source: Importantly, the Nfs1 and Isd11 protein that remain in these cells is found only in insoluble aggregates in contrast to WT cells where Nfs1 and Isd11 are soluble (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In WT cells, Nfs1 and Isd11 are soluble.
source: Importantly, the Nfs1 and Isd11 protein that remain in these cells is found only in insoluble aggregates in contrast to WT cells where Nfs1 and Isd11 are soluble (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the absence of Acp1, the Nfs1-Isd11 complex is destabilized, most likely causing a loss of cysteine desulfurase activity.
source: Thus, in the absence of Acp1, the Nfs1-Isd11 complex is destabilized, most likely causing a loss of cysteine desulfurase activity.
evidence: Inferred from the destabilization of the complex and aggregation of its subunits.

claim: Depletion of ACP in C2C12 mouse myoblasts is accompanied by a destabilization of the subunits of the mammalian FeS biogenesis machinery, NFS1, ISD11, and ISCU2.
source: While our methods were unable to detect the mammalian Nfs1-Isd11 complex by BN-PAGE, depletion of ACP in these cells was accompanied by a clear destabilization of the subunits of the mammalian FeS biogenesis machinery, NFS1, ISD11, and ISCU2, which is the mammalian version of Isu1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ISCU2 is the mammalian version of Isu1.
source: While our methods were unable to detect the mammalian Nfs1-Isd11 complex by BN-PAGE, depletion of ACP in these cells was accompanied by a clear destabilization of the subunits of the mammalian FeS biogenesis machinery, NFS1, ISD11, and ISCU2, which is the mammalian version of Isu1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about mammalian FeS biogenesis proteins.

claim: ACP plays an evolutionarily conserved role in stabilizing the ISU complex thereby enabling FeS biogenesis.
source: Thus, ACP plays an evolutionarily conserved role in stabilizing the ISU complex thereby enabling FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data in both yeast and mammalian cells.

claim: Overexpression of the MRS3 iron transporter resulted in robust stabilization of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of the MRS3 iron transporter resulted in robust stabilization of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells, while not restoring lipoic acid biosynthesis (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Overexpression of MRS3 does not restore lipoic acid biosynthesis in Acp1KD cells.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of the MRS3 iron transporter resulted in robust stabilization of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells, while not restoring lipoic acid biosynthesis (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Elevated Mrs3 expression restored Sdh2 and Rip1 protein abundance and complex assembly in Acp1KD cells.
source: Elevated Mrs3 expression also restored Sdh2 and Rip1 protein abundance and complex assembly as well as aconitase activity in Acp1KD cells (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Elevated Mrs3 expression restored aconitase activity in Acp1KD cells.
source: Elevated Mrs3 expression also restored Sdh2 and Rip1 protein abundance and complex assembly as well as aconitase activity in Acp1KD cells (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Elevated levels of Isu1 yielded a modest stabilization of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells.
source: Elevated levels of Isu1 yielded a modest stabilization and restored aconitase activity (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), while overexpression of Yfh1, the yeast frataxin homologue, had no effect (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Elevated levels of Isu1 restored aconitase activity in Acp1KD cells.
source: Elevated levels of Isu1 yielded a modest stabilization and restored aconitase activity (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), while overexpression of Yfh1, the yeast frataxin homologue, had no effect (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Overexpression of Yfh1, the yeast frataxin homologue, had no effect on the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells.
source: Elevated levels of Isu1 yielded a modest stabilization and restored aconitase activity (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), while overexpression of Yfh1, the yeast frataxin homologue, had no effect (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Elevated Mrs3 may increase the Fe(II) occupancy of Isu1, which enables it to more effectively stabilize the ISU complex.
source: We speculate that elevated Mrs3 may increase the Fe(II) occupancy of Isu1, which enables it to more effectively stabilize the ISU complex.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations.

claim: Acp1 requires a 4-PP prosthetic group to support mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis.
source: Acp1 requires a 4-PP prosthetic group to support mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about ACP function.

claim: The gene encoding 4-PP transferase, PPT2, is not essential.
source: The gene encoding 4-PP transferase, PPT2, is not essential, but the haploid deletion strain exhibits no growth in respiration-requiring medium and impaired growth on glucose, which does not require respiration (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The ppt2Δ haploid deletion strain exhibits no growth in respiration-requiring medium.
source: The gene encoding 4-PP transferase, PPT2, is not essential, but the haploid deletion strain exhibits no growth in respiration-requiring medium and impaired growth on glucose, which does not require respiration (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The ppt2Δ haploid deletion strain exhibits impaired growth on glucose.
source: The gene encoding 4-PP transferase, PPT2, is not essential, but the haploid deletion strain exhibits no growth in respiration-requiring medium and impaired growth on glucose, which does not require respiration (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The growth impairment of ppt2Δ on glucose may relate to defects in FeS biogenesis.
source: The growth impairment on glucose is not explained by any known function of ACP and therefore may relate to defects in FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations.

claim: Apo-Acp1 can be generated in vivo by mutating the invariant Ser (S82) to which 4-PP is conjugated.
source: Apo-Acp1 can be generated in vivo by mutating the invariant Ser (S82) to which 4-PP is conjugated (Stuible et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Re-expression of WT Acp1 fully restored the steady state abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells.
source: While re-expression of WT Acp1 could fully restore the steady state abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells, expression of Acp1S82A had only modest effects (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Expression of Acp1S82A had only modest effects on the steady state abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells.
source: While re-expression of WT Acp1 could fully restore the steady state abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex in Acp1KD cells, expression of Acp1S82A had only modest effects (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The modest effects of Acp1S82A were sufficient to enable the Acp1KD cells to retain viability, albeit with impaired growth rate.
source: These modest effects were sufficient to enable the Acp1KD cells expressing Acp1S82A to retain viability, albeit with impaired grow rate, and to exhibit a modest recovery of aconitase activity compared to Acp1KD cells (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Acp1KD cells expressing Acp1S82A exhibit a modest recovery of aconitase activity compared to Acp1KD cells.
source: These modest effects were sufficient to enable the Acp1KD cells expressing Acp1S82A to retain viability, albeit with impaired grow rate, and to exhibit a modest recovery of aconitase activity compared to Acp1KD cells (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The apparent absence of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex on BN gels in cells expressing Acp1S82A is likely the result of a severely destabilized complex that is not capable of surviving the stringent detergent conditions of BN-PAGE.
source: Thus, the apparent absence of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex on BN gels is likely the result of a severely destabilized complex that is not capable of surviving the stringent detergent conditions of BN-PAGE and not the complete loss of the complex in vivo.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental observations of viability and modest activity recovery.

claim: The Nfs1-Isd11 complex was severely depleted in ppt2Δ cells.
source: Like Acp1KD cells expressing Acp1S82A, the Nfs1-Isd11 complex was severely depleted in ppt2Δ cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: ppt2Δ cells exhibit a diminution in activity of FeS-containing enzymes in both the mitochondria and cytosol.
source: Furthermore, these cells exhibit a clear diminution in activity of FeS-containing enzymes in both the mitochondria and cytosol as represented by aconitase and sulfite reductase activity, respectively (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: The steady state levels of Acp1 are not affected in ppt2Δ cells.
source: While the steady state levels of Acp1 are not affected in ppt2Δ cells (Figure 4C), we observed a clear defect in the ability of Acp1 to interact with Nfs1 in this strain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: There is a clear defect in the ability of Acp1 to interact with Nfs1 in ppt2Δ cells.
source: While the steady state levels of Acp1 are not affected in ppt2Δ cells (Figure 4C), we observed a clear defect in the ability of Acp1 to interact with Nfs1 in this strain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Acp1-conjugated 4-PP plays an important role in the interaction of Acp1 with the core Nfs1-Isd11 complex.
source: Therefore, the Acp1-conjugated 4-PP plays an important role in the interaction of Acp1 with the core Nfs1-Isd11 complex and in FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing defects in interaction and FeS biogenesis in ppt2Δ cells.

claim: The Acp1-conjugated 4-PP plays an important role in FeS biogenesis.
source: Therefore, the Acp1-conjugated 4-PP plays an important role in the interaction of Acp1 with the core Nfs1-Isd11 complex and in FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the experimental data showing defects in FeS biogenesis in ppt2Δ cells.

claim: lip5Δ cells cannot synthesize lipoic acid but remain competent for Acp1-dependent fatty acid synthesis.
source: Importantly, lip5Δ cells, which cannot synthesize lipoic acid but remain competent for Acp1-dependent fatty acid synthesis (Hiltunen et al., 2010), maintain normal abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex and aconitase and sulfide reductase activity (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C–E and cited reference.

claim: lip5Δ cells maintain normal abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex.
source: Importantly, lip5Δ cells, which cannot synthesize lipoic acid but remain competent for Acp1-dependent fatty acid synthesis (Hiltunen et al., 2010), maintain normal abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex and aconitase and sulfide reductase activity (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C–E.

claim: lip5Δ cells maintain normal aconitase activity.
source: Importantly, lip5Δ cells, which cannot synthesize lipoic acid but remain competent for Acp1-dependent fatty acid synthesis (Hiltunen et al., 2010), maintain normal abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex and aconitase and sulfide reductase activity (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C–E.

claim: lip5Δ cells maintain normal sulfite reductase activity.
source: Importantly, lip5Δ cells, which cannot synthesize lipoic acid but remain competent for Acp1-dependent fatty acid synthesis (Hiltunen et al., 2010), maintain normal abundance of the Nfs1-Isd11 complex and aconitase and sulfide reductase activity (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C–E.

claim: The defects in FeS biogenesis observed in cells expressing apo-Acp1 are a result of the inability to generate an acyl-conjugated Acp1 species and not a defect in lipoic acid biosynthesis.
source: Thus, the defects in FeS biogenesis observed in cells expressing apo-Acp1 are a result of the inability to generate an acyl-conjugated Acp1 species and not a defect in lipoic acid biosynthesis.
evidence: Inferred from the comparison of ppt2Δ and lip5Δ cells.

claim: ACP functions as a stable subunit of the ISU complex where it acts to stabilize the complex in part by exploiting a 4-PP-conjugated acyl chain.
source: ACP functions as a stable subunit of the ISU complex where it acts to stabilize the complex in part by exploiting a 4-PP-conjugated acyl chain.
evidence: Inferred from the combined experimental data showing interaction, stabilization, and the role of 4-PP.

claim: The acyl chain is not absolutely required for FeS biogenesis and viability.
source: Unlike ACP, however, the acyl chain is not absolutely required for FeS biogenesis and viability, which raises the intriguing possibility that ACP is not simply an obligate subunit, but may exploit this unique interaction modality to provide additional structural or regulatory functions on FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the viability of cells expressing Acp1S82A.

claim: ACP may exploit its unique interaction modality to provide additional structural or regulatory functions on FeS biogenesis.
source: Unlike ACP, however, the acyl chain is not absolutely required for FeS biogenesis and viability, which raises the intriguing possibility that ACP is not simply an obligate subunit, but may exploit this unique interaction modality to provide additional structural or regulatory functions on FeS biogenesis.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations.

claim: ACP may serve to coordinate mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis and FeS biogenesis.
source: It is particularly intriguing to speculate that ACP may serve to coordinate mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis and FeS biogenesis, which represent two critical biosynthetic processes performed by mitochondria.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the dual role of ACP in both pathways.

claim: Mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis and FeS biogenesis represent two critical biosynthetic processes performed by mitochondria.
source: It is particularly intriguing to speculate that ACP may serve to coordinate mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis and FeS biogenesis, which represent two critical biosynthetic processes performed by mitochondria.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about mitochondrial biosynthetic processes.

claim: ACP utilizes a 4'-phosphopantetheine prosthetic group (4-PP), which is covalently bound to an invariant Ser residue.
source: To facilitate FASII, ACP utilizes a 4'-phosphopantetheine prosthetic group (4-PP), which is covalently bound to an invariant Ser residue (Majerus et al., 1965; Stuible et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: ACP serves as a soluble scaffold for acyl intermediates during the stepwise process of de novo fatty acid synthesis.
source: As such, ACP serves as a soluble scaffold for acyl intermediates during the stepwise process of de novo fatty acid synthesis.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about ACP function.

claim: The primary product of ACP-dependent FASII is octanoate, which is cleaved from ACP and further processed to generate lipoic acid.
source: Currently, it is thought that the primary product of ACP-dependent FASII is octanoate, which is cleaved from ACP and further processed to generate lipoic acid.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about FASII.

claim: Lipoic acid is an obligate cofactor of the pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes as well as the branched chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase and glycine cleavage complex.
source: Lipoic acid is an obligate cofactor of the pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complexes as well as the branched chain α-keto acid dehydrogenase and glycine cleavage complex (Hiltunen et al., 2010; Brody et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by cited references.

claim: A FASII-derived acyl chain other than lipoic acid is required for RNase P function in tRNA maturation.
source: In addition, a FASII-derived acyl chain other than lipoic acid is required for RNase P function in tRNA maturation (Schonauer et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by cited reference.

claim: Mammalian FASII enzymes are capable of generating ACP-bound acyl chains as long as fourteen carbons.
